text: Git is a version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build new features safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the main code stable and makes teamwork easier. By using branches, merging, and pull requests, developers can collaborate smoothly and avoid mistakes in their projects.
